free_tier.stated: Five files a day and a 1.2 GB maximum file size, on free hosts only. The logged-out downloader page shows the panel 'Files per day 0 / 5', 'Filenext Files 0 / 3' and 'Maximum File Sizes: General 1.2 GB, Filenext 300.0 MB, Emload 300.0 MB'.
free_tier.notes: The home page states the same rule in prose: 'With the free account you will be able to fetch up to 5 cloud provider links every day.'

per_object_cap.stated: 1.2 GB per file generally; 300 MB on Filenext and Emload

retention.stated: not applicable: no storage is offered on the free account; downloads are proxied for a user

egress.terms: Five files a day at a 1.2 GB maximum is 6 GB a day, 180 GB a month, if every file lands at the cap. The site also warns that 'some providers have daily limits' even on paid plans.

interface_detail: REST API v1 (https://www.deepbrid.com/api/v1) with an apikey, documented publicly, including a /user/limits endpoint.
tooling: Documented REST API with per-account rate limits and X-RateLimit headers; browser extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Opera and Edge; a WebDAV path advertised in the integrations strip.
chaining: Enough to fetch a handful of small files a day from hosts a user does not subscribe to, and not enough for anything larger than a 1.2 GB file, which rules out most media and any dataset.

limits.value: 1.2 GB per file; 300 MB on Filenext and Emload

limits_note: The 1.2 GB figure is a per-file ceiling, not a daily total, so a 5 GB video cannot be fetched at all on this tier regardless of how many files remain.
binding_note: The 5-file daily counter allows 180 GB a month, which is, but the per-file cap is what a reader meets first: any object above 1.2 GB is refused outright, so no amount of patience recovers it.

identity_cost.detail: E-mail account; the signup page states 'No credit card required for free accounts'.

reliability_note: The account is free but capped on both axes; the site's own status page says free and guest users see only free hosters with restrictions, and the terms allow automatic suspension without notice.
confidence_note: The limits panel is rendered by the vendor's own downloader page for a logged-out session, so both numbers are read from the live site. Whether the 1.2 GB is enforced per file or per day is the vendor's wording, taken as written.

notes: The numbers are on the vendor's own downloader page and the per-file cap is the one that matters: it is the only service whose free tier refuses a file by size rather than by count. The ladder multiplies 5 x 1.2 x 30 = 180 GB, which stands as a per-session ceiling but is not proven repeatable across two accounts or two addresses.
